items.longBusinessSummary: Marvell Technology, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides data infrastructure semiconductor solutions and spanning the data center core to network edge in the United States, Argentina, China, India, Israel, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Vietnam, and internationally. The company develops and scales system-on-a-chip architectures, integrating analog, mixed-signal, and digital signal processing functionality. It offers a portfolio of ethernet solutions, including spanning controllers, network adapters, physical transceivers, and switches; single or multiple core processors; and custom application specific integrated circuits, interconnects, fibre channel adapters, and processors. The company also provides interconnect products, including pulse amplitude modulation, coherent and coherent-lite digital signal processors (DSPs), laser drivers, trans-impedance amplifiers, silicon photonics, co-packaged optics, linear pluggable optics chipsets, data center interconnect, active electrical cable DSPs and peripheral component interconnect express retimer solutions; fibre channel products comprising host bus adapters and controllers for server and storage system connectivity; storage controllers for hard disk drives and solid-state-drives; host system interfaces, including serial advanced technology attachment and serial attached SCSI, peripheral component interconnect express, compute express link switches, non-volatile memory express (NVMe), and NVMe over fabrics; and develops ultra accelerator linkTM switches and ethernet for scale-up networking switches. The company serves data centers, communications, and other markets. It offers its products through direct customers and distributors. Marvell Technology, Inc. was incorporated in 1995 and is headquartered in Wilmington, Delaware.

surviving corporation (the “Surviving Corporation”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the

The Merger On November 1, 2026, Marvell
Technology, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Marvell”) entered into an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the “Merger Agreement”) with Lumentum Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation (“Lumentum”),
Java Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub I”) and Java Merger Sub II, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell (“Merger Sub
II” and together with Merger Sub I, each a “Merger Sub” and collectively the “Merger Subs”). Upon the
terms and subject to the conditions of the Merger Agreement, Merger Sub I will merge with and into Lumentum (the “First Merger”), with Lumentum continuing as the surviving corporation (the “Surviving
Corporation”) and as a wholly owned subsidiary of Marvell, and promptly following the Effective Time (as defined below), the Surviving Corporation will merge with and into Merger Sub II (the “Second Merger” and,
collectively or in seriatim with the First Merger, as applicable, the “Merger”), with Merger Sub II continuing as the surviving corporation of the Second Merger (the “Second Surviving Corporation”).
The board of directors of Marvell (the “Marvell Board”) has unanimously: (i) approved and declared advisable the Merger Agreement and
the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement, including the Merger, an amendment of Marvell’s Second Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation (the “Charter”) to increase the number of authorized shares of
Marvell Common Stock thereunder (the “Charter Amendment”), the issuance of the shares of Marvell Common Stock and, if applicable, Marvell Series B Preferred Stock, in connection with the Merger (the “Share
Issuance”), (ii) determined that the Merger Agreement and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the Merger, the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance, are fair to, and in the best interests of, Marvell and its stockholders,
and (iii) resolved to recommend that Marvell’s stockholders approve the Charter Amendment and the Share Issuance. Merger Consideration
At the effective time of the First Merger (the “Effective Time”), each share of common stock, par value $0.001 per share, of
Lumentum (the “Lumentum Common Stock”) that is issued and outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive 4.500 shares of
common stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the “Marvell Common Stock,” and such ratio, the “Exchange Ratio”), with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common Stock payable in accordance with
the Merger Agreement (the “Common Stock Merger Consideration”). At the Effective Time, each share of preferred stock, par value $0.001
per share, of Lumentum designated as Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock” and, together with the Lumentum Common Stock, the “Lumentum Capital Stock”) that is issued and
outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time, subject to certain exceptions in the Merger Agreement, will be converted into the right to receive a number of shares of Marvell Common Stock equal to the product of (a) the number of shares
of Lumentum Common Stock into which such share of Lumentum Preferred Stock is convertible pursuant to its terms as of immediately prior to the Effective Time and (b) the Exchange Ratio, with cash in lieu of fractional shares of Marvell Common
Stock payable in accordance with the Merger Agreement (the “Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration”). However, if a holder of
shares of Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock makes an election in accordance with the terms of the Merger Agreement to receive the Merger Consideration in the form of Series B Convertible Preferred Stock, par value $0.002 per share, of Marvell (the
“Marvell Series B Preferred Stock,” and such election, a “Preferred Stock Election”), then each share of Lumentum Preferred Stock that is held by such holder immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead
be converted into the right to receive one share of Marvell Series B Preferred Stock (the “Series B Preferred Stock Merger Consideration” and together with the Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration and the Common Stock
Merger Consideration, the “Merger Consideration”). The Marvell Series B Preferred Stock is intended to have the same terms and rights as the Lumentum Series A Preferred Stock, except that each share is convertible for the
Preferred Common Stock Merger Consideration.

The shares of Marvell Common Stock to be issued in connection with the Merger will be listed on the Nasdaq
Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”). In connection with the issuance of the Merger Consideration by Marvell, as promptly as reasonably practicable following the date of the Merger Agreement, Marvell and Lumentum will jointly prepare
and cause to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”) a registration statement on Form S-4 (the “Form
S-4”), which will include the joint proxy statement of Marvell and Lumentum for their respective meetings of stockholders relating to the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement.
Treatment of Equity Awards Under the terms of the
Merger Agreement, each Lumentum equity award, consisting of stock options, restricted stock units and performance stock units, that is outstanding immediately prior to the Effective Time will be converted into an equivalent Marvell equity award,
including with respect to vesting conditions (including termination protection and provisions, expiration and post-termination exercisability), except that performance stock units will be converted into solely time-vesting restricted stock units.
The number of shares of Marvell Common Stock subject to each converted equity award will be equal to the number of shares of Lumentum Common Stock then subject to the award (with the number of shares subject to any performance stock unit determined
based on (i) the greater of target and actual performance levels for stock price performance metrics and (ii) except as otherwise provided by the terms of Lumentum’s Change in Control and Severance Benefits Plan, as amended and
restated, that would apply assuming a participant’s qualifying termination of employment upon the consummation of the Merger, at projected actual performance for all other performance metrics measured through the Effective Time), multiplied
by the Exchange Ratio, and the exercise price of each converted stock option will be equal to the exercise price of the Lumentum stock option divided by the Exchange Ratio.
Notwithstanding the foregoing, each restricted stock unit of Lumentum that is outstanding and held by a non-employee
director as of immediately prior to the Effective Time will instead be cancelled and converted into the right to receive the Common Stock Merger Consideration.

nominate each such designee who is still serving for election at Marvell’s first annual meeting of stockholders following the Effective Time.

Item 1.01
Entry into a Material Definitive Agreement. Third Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Agreement On October 22, 2026, Marvell Technology, Inc. (the “Company”) entered into that certain Third Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Agreement (the “Revolving Credit Agreement”), by and among the Company, as borrower, the lenders party thereto (each, a “Revolving Lender”) and Bank of America, N.A. (the “Administrative Agent”), as the administrative agent. The Revolving Credit Agreement provides for borrowings of up to $3 billion in the form of revolving loans (“Revolving Loans”). Subject to certain conditions, the Company may increase the commitments under the Revolving Credit Agreement by up to an aggregate of $2 billion. The proceeds of the Revolving Loans may be used for working capital in the ordinary course of business and general corporate purposes of the Company and its subsidiaries. The Revolving Credit Agreement amends and restates in its entirety that certain Second Amended and Restated Revolving Credit Agreement, dated as of June 30, 2025, by and among the Company, the lenders from time to time party thereto and the Administrative Agent, which provided for a $1.5 billion revolving credit facility maturing June 2030. As of the effective date of the Revolving Credit Agreement, no Revolving Loans were outstanding. Amounts borrowed under the Revolving Credit Agreement bear interest, at the Company’s election, at an “alternate base rate” plus an applicable margin, a term SOFR rate with a term of one, three or six months, plus an applicable margin, or a daily SOFR rate plus an applicable margin. The “alternate base rate” is a per annum rate equal to the highest of (i) 0.5% above the federal funds effective rate, (ii) the prime rate set by the administrative agent, (iii) 1.0% above the one-month term SOFR rate and (iv) 1.0%. The applicable margin for “alternate base rate” loans ranges from 0.0% to 0.5% and the applicable margin for term SOFR and daily SOFR loans ranges from 0.875% to 1.5%, in each case, with the actual margin determined according to the Company’s debt ratings. The Company must pay each Revolving Lender an unused commitment fee, which accrues based on the Company’s debt ratings and ranges from 0.075% to 0.20% per annum. The commitments under the Revolving Credit Agreement terminate, and all Revolving Loans must be repaid, on the fifth anniversary of the effective date of the Revolving Credit Agreement; provided, however, that subject to certain conditions, the Company may request that the Revolving Lenders extend the maturity date by one year. Revolving Loans may be voluntarily prepaid in full or in part at any time, subject to customary breakage costs, if applicable. Title: Micron Falls 4% as Kioxia’s Cautious Outlook Hits Memory Stocks; Western Digital Drops 5%, SanDisk Slides 3%
Author: David Moadel   Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:53 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-11-02T18:53:55+00:00
=== BODY ===
Kioxia's below-estimate December-quarter guidance sent Micron down 4% and Western Digital down 5%, extending both stocks' month-long losses past 20%.
Citrini analyst Jukan read Lumentum's sale to Marvell as a signal management expects the AI cycle to collapse within two to three years.
Kioxia CFO Kawamura called the soft outlook a shipment timing issue, saying AI demand stays robust and next year's output is already sold out.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and Micron Technology didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat MU. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
A cautious forecast from Kioxia Holdings, Japan's largest memory chipmaker, turned an overnight gain in Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) into a loss and pulled memory stocks lower. Micron stock is at $853.34, down 4% this afternoon. The decline adds to a pullback from an AI-fueled run in the chipmaker's shares.
Over the past month, Micron stock is down 20%. That slide comes despite record results: on September 30, the company reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of $54.23 billion, up 379.3% year over year, with an adjusted gross margin of 87%. For Q1 FY2027, Micron forecast its revenue to $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion.
Kioxia Holdings guided its December-quarter operating profit to 2 trillion yen, the company said on November 2. That forecast stands only slightly above the 1.99 trillion yen Kioxia earned in the September quarter, and it came in below analyst estimates. Shares of Kioxia declined in Tokyo as investors digested the outlook.
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
The company attributed the soft outlook mainly to shipment timing, saying some orders were pulled into the September quarter while others were pushed into the March quarter. Chief Financial Officer Yoshihiko Kawamura said Kioxia expects a return to rapid growth in the March quarter. He added that AI data center demand remains robust and that Kioxia has sold out its planned output for next year.
Micron's slide also follows a weak prior session on October 30, when Samsung missed profit expectations. The open question for the group is whether Kioxia's outlook signals cooling AI memory demand and pricing, or whether the selling reflects broader tech positioning.
Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) stock is at $347.24, down 5%. That's a steeper decline than Micron's, making the hard drive maker the weakest of the three. During the past month, Western Digital has lost 24%. The company sells to hyperscalers, cloud service providers and enterprises building out storage for the AI-driven data economy.
SanDisk (NASDAQ:SNDK) stock is at $1,114.65, down 3%. The flash maker is falling less than Micron, which cuts against the idea that Kioxia's manufacturing partner would take the hardest hit. Across the past month, SanDisk has dropped 36%, the deepest decline in the group, and it declined in the prior session despite upbeat results reported on October 29.
Micron makes dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) along with NAND and NOR flash, including high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for AI systems. The company's Strategic Customer Agreements are designed to secure long-term demand visibility, particularly for AI workloads. This mix links Micron to both major memory markets at once.
Western Digital now operates as a hard disk drive company after separating its flash business into SanDisk, and it keeps an ownership interest in SanDisk. SanDisk, by contrast, designs and makes NAND flash and solid-state drives, producing wafers through Flash Ventures, its joint venture arrangements with Kioxia. That arrangement links SanDisk most directly to Kioxia's production, while Micron's DRAM exposure gives it pricing drivers that NAND-focused peers don't share.
Micron's upcoming earnings report will show whether pricing momentum holds up. On the September 30 call, President and Chief Operating Officer Manish Bhatia said Micron doesn't have "line of sight to when supply and demand balance." The company also noted it had "more than 75% of our shipments committed for the year." Kioxia's comments on order timing and sold-out output add support to that view.
Skeptics see a cycle nearing its peak. Analysts' average revenue estimate for Micron's fiscal year ending August 2027 is $275.5 billion, a high bar. Citrini Research analyst Jukan has read the sale of Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) to Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) as a sign that management expects the AI cycle to "collapse in two to three years," a view that remains one analyst's take.
Another weak stretch for the memory group could deepen Micron's monthly losses, while a pricing update matching Kioxia's upbeat March commentary could ease the pressure. A cautious approach may make sense until the memory-demand debate resolves.

Title: Marvell Stocks Decline 6.8% With Lumentum Deal Putting Dilution Ahead of Synergies
Author: Khac Phu Nguyen   Mon, November 2, 2026 at 7:54 PM GMT+1 1 min read
Published: 2026-11-02T18:54:01+00:00
=== BODY ===
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Marvell (NASDAQ:MRVL), the custom-chip and data-center connectivity supplier, fell 6.82% to $183 at 10:05 a.m. ET on November 2 as its proposed Lumentum acquisition put dilution front and center. The proposed combination would expand Marvell's reach in optical connectivity for AI data centers. But a bigger business must deliver more earnings per share to give existing investors a compelling payoff.
Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MRVL.
Is MRVL fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.
The November 2 agreement values Lumentum at $115 billion including debt, with holders receiving 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share. Existing Marvell owners would hold approximately 67% of the combined company. Management expects the transaction to lift adjusted earnings per share in the first year after closing and projects more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost savings. Closing is expected in the first half of 2028, leaving a lengthy stretch before those promises face their delivery test.
The valuation leaves little room for disappointment. GuruFocus shows an 81/100 GF Score, with growth the strongest dimension and GF Value the weakest; a price-to-earnings ratio of 60.26 adds pressure to execute. A shareholder owning 1% of Marvell would own roughly 0.67% of the enlarged company, before other ownership changes. That smaller percentage could still represent greater economic value if Lumentum brings enough earnings and assets. Approvals, integration spending and delivery of the projected savings could determine whether this AI expansion earns its price.
